payload.subject: Consolidated blocker report: symptom, Defect A, host-indexer trigger (all verified), Defect C corroborated with a measured 5-slot leak, plus NEW guard-gap finding - no deadline anywhere on the vault-read path. Retest requires indexer-clear THEN restart. Correcting my own stale 'unowned' claim: claude owns it. Holding.
payload.body_markdown:
Consolidated report on the release blocker at owner instruction, then I hold for instructions and start nothing.

Everything below is either verified by me at merged main `b0c7ee2` or attributed to the peer who established it. Where I verified a peer's claim myself I say so, because this root has repeatedly propagated unverified claims between agents this week.

# 1. Correction to my own seq 11 first

My seq 11 said Defect B was **open and unowned in practice**. **That is now stale and was stale within 90 minutes.** claude-fable-gkos took it at seq 16 (17:27Z), falsified their own hypothesis at seq 17 (17:43Z), and added evidence at seq 18 (18:14Z). I also told the owner it was unowned. Correcting both: **claude owns the blocker and is actively working it.**

This is the fourth time this week I have reported a state that had already changed. The pattern is consistent: I report, then read.

# 2. What is now established about the blocker

## 2.1 The symptom (JEFFREY seq 15, 16:06Z)

Client gate against live v0.8.3: **PARTIAL PASS, release-blocked.** Metadata plane fully conformant -- `server/discover` and `tools/list` 200 in 0.01-0.02s with `cacheScope: private` / `ttlMs: 0`, strict Python SDK wire validation **passes**, Hermes negotiates `DiscoverResult@2026-07-28` and lists 18 tools. **His #51 fix is confirmed live and wire-valid.**

Every vault-backed read dies: `/notes`, `/note`, `/overview`, `search_notes`, `vault_overview` -- all `RemoteDisconnected` at 30.0-30.3s. Search, allowed read, restricted denial and traversal are unreachable, so the gate **cannot pass**.

## 2.2 Defect A -- the silent socket kill (dale seq 16; I verified independently)

Verified by grep at `b0c7ee2`:

- `agent-server.ts:263` -- `export const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;`
- `agent-server.ts:582` -- `if (typeof srv.setTimeout === "function") srv.setTimeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS);`
- **zero** `'timeout'` listeners in the file.

Node destroys a timed-out socket when nothing listens for `'timeout'`: no status line, no body. That is `RemoteDisconnected` at ~30s, matching JEFFREY's 30.03 / 30.0 / 30.01 / 30.0 exactly. **Confirmed.** It is a diagnosability defect in its own right -- JEFFREY had to rule out rate-limiting by reasoning about what a 429 would have looked like, because the server destroys the evidence along with the connection.

## 2.3 The trigger is the host, not our code (claude seq 17; I verified the load-bearing claim)

claude tested against a server the owner restarted with **no fixes**, and falsified their own seq 16 hypothesis:

    health              200   0.07s
    root                200   0.01s
    call 1 /overview    FAIL  30.03s   socket killed
    call 2 /overview    FAIL  30.01s   socket killed

**The first call after a clean restart hangs**, so no serve-then-pin transition can be the cause. And it never completes: t=0 fail, +150s quiet fail, +150s quiet fail. A rebuild merely taking 60-120s would have finished during 300s of quiet. **The vault plane is stuck, not slow.**

Owner screenshots show Obsidian's own persistent notice -- *"Indexing vault... Some functionality may not be available until this is complete"* -- displayed throughout. **I verified the decisive claim myself:** `git grep -c "Indexing vault" origin/main -- src` returns **zero**. That string is not ours. It is the host application's indexer, and it was running while every vault read died.

claude also corrected a fact they had stated loosely: 192.168.5.95 is the **same Windows host** they run on, so their local measurements are same-machine, same-vault, same-disk rather than an approximation.

## 2.4 Defect C -- the concurrency leak (mine, seq 11; corroborated with a measured count by claude seq 18)

`agent-server.ts:1409`: `this.inFlight++`, `await this.dispatch(...)`, decrement in `finally`. **Destroying the socket does not settle the awaited promise.** If the graph read never resolves, `dispatch` never settles, the `finally` never runs, and neither `inFlight` nor `perAgentInFlight` is released. Node has discarded the connection; the handler is still awaiting.

With `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 24` (`:262`) and `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_AGENT = 12` (`:273`): 12 hangs from one client refuses that client everything; 24 total refuses everyone, including `/health`. Only a process restart clears it.

**claude seq 18 has measured an instance:** 5 hung vault calls since the owner's restart, so **~5 of 24 global slots and ~5 of 12 on their agent key are consumed.** They recorded it explicitly so a future 429 from their identity is not misread as a new defect. That is the right hygiene and it closes the loop on my finding with an observed count rather than a prediction.

## 2.5 NEW -- the guard gap, which I think is the actual shape of our defect

If the trigger is the host indexer, then the bug in **our** code is not the slowness. It is that **nothing on the vault-read path can notice, report, or recover from host-unreadiness.**

Verified at `b0c7ee2`:

- The renderer snapshot path (`main.ts:166-176`, `sendFull`) drives `getMarkdownFiles()` then `readBatches(md, ... await cachedRead(f) ...)` over the whole vault with **no per-file and no overall deadline**.
- The **only** `Promise.race`/`AbortController` in `main.ts` is at `:418`, unrelated to that loop.
- **Caveat on scope:** I verified this pattern in `main.ts`. The API's `getGraph()` is only an interface member in `agent-server.ts` (`:319`); its implementation is in `vault-provider.ts`, which I have **not** examined. So I have established the pattern in the renderer path and am inferring, not asserting, that the API path shares it. Whoever owns the provider should confirm rather than take this from me.

On that reading the three defects are facets of one requirement: **an unbounded await with no deadline (guard gap), which the socket layer then kills silently (A), leaking a slot each time (C).** A fix that adds a deadline to the vault path and returns a real error -- 503 with `Retry-After` and a body naming host-unreadiness -- would address the symptom, the diagnosability and the leak together, and would be honest about the fact that the host genuinely is not ready.

# 3. What is still NOT established

- **Why the read does not settle even after the indexer would plausibly have finished.** claude's 300s patience test argues it is stuck rather than slow, but the mechanism inside `cachedRead`/the provider under a mid-index host is not established. This is the remaining unknown and it is the release gate.
- **Whether the indexer clearing is sufficient** to make the gate pass. Nobody has yet observed a vault read succeed on this build with the notice cleared. Until someone does, "host was indexing" is the leading explanation, not a closed one.
- **The live build's commit is unverified** (dale seq 18). The server self-reports v0.8.3 but nobody has tied the running process to a commit, so strictly we do not know the deployed tree equals `b0c7ee2`.

# 4. What is needed

1. **Wait for Obsidian's "Indexing vault..." notice to clear, confirm it has cleared, restart the server, then re-run the gate.** Both claude seq 17/18 and my seq 11 converge on this. A measurement taken while the notice is displayed measures the host indexer; a measurement taken without a restart is polluted by leaked slots. **Order matters and both steps are required.**
2. **A decision on whether the guard gap is in scope for 0.8.3** or is a follow-up. If the release can qualify once the host is idle, the guard is a hardening item. If the release must survive a mid-index host, it is a blocker in its own right. **That is an owner call, not a lane call** -- it is a question about what the release promises.
3. **Confirmation of the deployed commit**, so the gate evidence is anchored to a tree.
4. **Lane clarity on the guard gap if it is taken:** the deadline belongs on the vault path (`vault-provider.ts`, codex) while the socket handling and the leak are in `agent-server.ts` (claude). One requirement, two owners, one review gate.

# 5. My standing

My assigned item -- R1 normative verification, per JEFFREY seq 14 -- is **delivered and closed** (seq 9, corrected at seq 10). `acks/carl/` was empty since registration; I have now written all 30 with per-message reasons and verified every `message_sha256` against raw bytes, and the 4 that arrived since will follow.

**I hold nothing, claim nothing, and have touched no code.** All three defects are in other lanes. I am not taking the guard gap, not touching `agent-server.ts` or `vault-provider.ts`, and not re-running the gate against the live server on another lane's host.

**Awaiting instructions.**
